Generation contract and downloads

Source: vignettes/articles/generation-contract.Rmd
generation-contract.Rmd

This guide describes the prompt and normalization code inspected on 2026-10-14. It separates what the model is asked to produce from what the application checks.

Package return values

generate_sas_tests() without a callback returns an offline list containing prompt, requirements, macro, an empty test_cases data frame, and an empty sas_code character vector. With a callback, it returns the callback’s value unchanged.

generate_sas_tests_openrouter() returns:

Field Value
model Requested model identifier
prompt Prompt containing the FRD and macro source
response Raw model response text
parsed JSON decoded with simplifyVector = FALSE, or NULL when decoding fails

Provider and authentication errors propagate from ellmer. Invalid JSON does not itself raise a package error: parsed becomes NULL. The package does not enforce the requested output schema after decoding.

Requested JSON

The system prompt requests these top-level fields: test_cases, sample_data, sas_code, sas_test_code, and traceability. Each test case is requested to contain exactly Test_ID, Requirement_ID, Test_Type, Test_Scenario, Input, and Expected_Result.

The following is an illustrative shape, not a recorded model response or an executed SAS test:

{
  "test_cases": [
    {
      "Test_ID": "TC001",
      "Requirement_ID": "FRD-001",
      "Test_Type": "POSITIVE",
      "Test_Scenario": "A BASELINE visit receives the baseline flag",
      "Input": "VISIT = BASELINE",
      "Expected_Result": "BASEFL = Y"
    }
  ],
  "sample_data": [{"VISIT": "BASELINE"}],
  "sas_code": "/* Draft SAS sample-data program */",
  "sas_test_code": "/* Draft SAS validation program */",
  "traceability": ["FRD-001 -> TC001"]
}

The prompt does not fully specify the nested sample-data or traceability schema, or establish a guaranteed division of responsibility between the two SAS files. Review both programs rather than inferring their contents from their filenames.

What the app accepts and displays

normalize_generated_result() requires a named response list and a named parsed list containing test_cases and sas_code. Both SAS fields are then normalized: character vectors are joined with newlines, and other values must pass a string assertion. Consequently, a missing sas_test_code also fails normalization, even though it is not named in the initial presence assertion.

The matrix has these six columns:

Column Current normalization
Test_ID Model value, or a generated TC001-style identifier
Requirement_ID Model value, or an empty string
Test_Type Model value, or an empty string
Test_Scenario Model value, or an empty string
Expected_Result Model value, or an empty string
Traceability Per-record value, otherwise the corresponding positional top-level entry, otherwise empty

Recognized alternative field spellings are handled by the code in normalize_test_cases() and as_text(). Missing descriptive fields can become empty cells. Input is requested from the model but is not displayed or included in the exported matrix. Extra test-case fields are also omitted from that matrix. Requirement IDs and traceability are not checked against the FRD or assessed for complete coverage.

sample_data can be a data frame, row-record list, column list, or scalar-like value. Missing sample data becomes an empty data frame. Row-record values are converted to strings and nested values joined with ;; uneven column lists are recycled to a common length. These conversions do not verify SAS variable types, input constraints, or consistency with the generated programs.

Downloads

The active download button creates Validation_Results.zip with:

File Contents
Validation_Test_Matrix.xlsx Validation_Matrix and Sample_Data worksheets
sas_code.sas Normalized model-supplied sas_code
sas_test_code.sas Normalized model-supplied sas_test_code

The workbook is written by writexl; ZIP creation uses utils::zip() and needs a working ZIP utility on the host. The app does not offer separate CSV or XLSX buttons. Those controls remain in the historical plan as an unresolved scope difference.

Failure and assurance boundaries

  • Missing credentials stop live generation. Invalid UI inputs receive field feedback. Provider errors and failed normalization are shown as notifications.
  • A caught generation error clears the result. Input changes and an early input-validation return can leave a previous result available; regenerate and confirm the correct input context before downloading.
  • Empty matrices can produce a display validation message; downloading only checks that a normalized result exists. Display status is not an approval gate.
  • The raw response is retained in the session result but is not exported. The ZIP also omits original inputs, prompt/model/settings, environment details, timestamps, and approval records. It is not a reproducibility or audit bundle.
  • JSON success and a populated matrix do not establish SAS syntax, execution, expected-result correctness, or requirement coverage. Low temperature does not guarantee identical model output.
  • The app sends the full FRD and SAS source to OpenRouter and its selected provider. It has no data-classification or de-identification control, enforced approval, durable evidence store, or SAS execution service.

For the input-to-export path and owning functions, read the architecture article.
